content.value_statement: Crypto market structure can be hard to compare across spot and futures data. This skill routes requests to Gate MCP market tools and returns structured analysis.
actual_capabilities: Routes ten market-analysis intents to documented spot or futures workflows.
Calls Gate MCP market data tools in defined orders for each scenario.
Calculates spread, slippage, top ten depth, volume comparisons, and liquidity ratings.
Screens funding arbitrage with funding rates, volume, spot-futures spread, and depth checks.
Builds reports for order books, liquidations, basis, support and resistance, and weekend versus weekday behavior.
Prompts for missing pair or quote amount before slippage simulations.
limitations: Requires Gate MCP to be configured and connected.
Provides data-based analysis only, not investment advice or trade execution.
Accuracy depends on returned Gate market data and endpoint availability.
Slippage simulations estimate market buy impact from visible order book levels only.

use_cases.title: Check trade liquidity
use_cases.description: Evaluate depth, spread, volume, and likely slippage before sizing a spot or futures trade.

use_cases.title: Monitor derivatives pressure
use_cases.description: Review funding, basis, liquidation, and momentum signals for BTC, ETH, or other Gate markets.

use_cases.title: Explain market structure
use_cases.description: Turn order book data into clear explanations of bids, asks, spread, support, and liquidity.

prompt_templates.title: Basic liquidity check
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze ETH liquidity on Gate spot. Show depth, spread, 24h volume, 30-day average volume, slippage risk, and a liquidity rating.

prompt_templates.title: Momentum review
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate spot or futures momentum analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare BTC perpetual momentum over the last 24 hours. Use buy and sell flow, volume, order book depth, and funding rate.

prompt_templates.title: Funding arbitrage screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Screen funding rate arbitrage candidates on Gate. Rank markets by funding rate, volume, spot-futures spread, and depth risk.

prompt_templates.title: Weekend liquidity study
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a weekend versus weekday liquidity review for ETH_USDT perpetual. Compare current depth with 90-day weekend and weekday volume and returns.

output_examples.output: A liquidity report with order book depth, 24-hour volume, 30-day average volume, spread, slippage risk, rating, and recommendation.

output_examples.input: ADA_USDT slippage simulation for a $10K market buy.
output_examples.output: A fill summary showing average fill price, amount filled, slippage versus best ask, and an execution risk conclusion.

output_examples.input: Is BTC perpetual funding arbitrage attractive?
output_examples.output: A funding analysis comparing funding rate, 24-hour volume, spot-futures spread, depth, and whether thin liquidity should exclude it.

best_practices: Provide the exact pair and market type when possible.
Include a quote amount for every slippage simulation.
Treat outputs as research inputs and validate with live data before decisions.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to place orders or manage positions.
Do not rely on reports when Gate MCP is disconnected or stale.
Do not request slippage simulation without a pair and quote amount.

faq.question: Does this skill place trades?
faq.answer: No. It only analyzes read-only market data and does not perform trading operations.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: Gate MCP must be configured and connected before the skill can request market data.

faq.question: Does it support futures markets?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses futures workflows when the prompt mentions perpetual, contract, or futures markets.

faq.question: What data can it analyze?
faq.answer: It can use order books, tickers, trades, candlesticks, funding rates, liquidations, and premium index data when available.

faq.question: Is the analysis investment advice?
faq.answer: No. The output is data-based market research and should not replace independent judgment.

faq.question: Why does slippage require a pair and amount?
faq.answer: Slippage depends on the selected order book and quote size, so defaults would produce unreliable estimates.
